title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book 1, Fugue 2 in C minor

sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Soprano: the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: the opening of countersubject 1 (4 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Returns in Episode 4 (bars 22–26).

sections.label: Episode 2
sections.summary: Soprano: the opening of countersubject 1, inverted (4 times), in a sequence rising by a step every bar. Alto: a figure from countersubject 1 (4 times), in a sequence rising by a step every bar. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1 (4 times), in a sequence rising by a step every bar.

sections.label: Episode 3
sections.summary: Reworks the codetta (bars 5–6) in part, with the soprano's line in the bass, the lines moved by different intervals (invertible counterpoint at the twelfth). Soprano: the opening of the subject (6 times), in a sequence rising by a step every half bar. Alto: the opening of countersubject 1, inverted (3 times) and the opening of the subject (3 times), in a sequence rising by a step every half bar. Bass: the opening of the subject (3 times) and the opening of countersubject 1, inverted (3 times), in a sequence rising by a step every half bar.

sections.label: Episode 4
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 1 (bars 9–10), in the same voices, a fifth lower. Soprano: the opening of the subject (5 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence rising by a step every half bar. Alto: the opening of the subject (2 times), in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: the opening of countersubject 1 (7 times) and the opening of countersubject 1, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every bar.

sections.label: Link
sections.summary: Soprano: the opening of countersubject 1. Alto: free counterpoint. Bass: a figure from countersubject 1, inverted.

sections.label: Final entry: Subject in C minor (Soprano), over a tonic pedal

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Soprano: the opening of the subject (3 times), in a sequence rising by a step every half bar. Alto: the opening of countersubject 1, inverted (2 times) and a figure from countersubject 1, in a sequence rising by a step every half bar. Returns in Episode 3 (bars 17–19).
